body:
## Downstream: formal-ai's self-translation blockers, one issue per construct, and a release request

formal-ai translates its JavaScript twins to Rust with `selfTranslate` at `679a3b3c` (PR #196). 249 of 2,369 top-level items translate today ([census](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/a75bf377287664599d506921a30bd3bc37410022/data/meta/js-rust-translation.lino)). Section 1 of this issue lists the constructs in general terms. Below is each one as its own issue, with formal-ai's count, a minimal JavaScript input checked against `679a3b3c`, and the Rust it should produce:

| issue | construct | carried items in formal-ai |
|---|---|---:|
| #203 | relative ESM imports | 417 |
| #208 | array methods (`.map/.filter/.find/.some/.push/…`, `Array.from`) | 324 |
| #204 | `null`/`undefined`/`??`/`?.` as `Option<T>` | 218 |
| #205 | JSDoc tuple/record/Map types, optional `[param]` | 210 |
| #202 | calls and reads of **sibling** top-level items (even translated ones) | 209 |
| #209 | string methods (`.split/.slice/.indexOf/.replace/…`) | 183 |
| #206 | plain object records, field reads, frozen namespaces | 129 |
| #210 | `new Set`/`new Map`, Error subclasses, classes | 110 |
| #207 | arrow functions/closures inside bodies | 99 |
| #211 | regex literals, **and a lexer bug** that reports them as `malformed number 9A` / `unterminated string literal` | 84 |
| #212 | `for (const [a] of …)`, string `case`, `try`, `typeof`, `let x;` | 62 |

#202 and the lexer half of #211 are the cheapest: most items behind #202 already use only portable constructs, and a function cannot use the module's own translated helpers and constants.

**Release request.** Please cut a release that contains PR #196: a crate and an npm package with `selfTranslate` / `self_translate`. The latest release is still 0.58.2 (2026-08-20), from before #196 was merged. Until a release exists, formal-ai pins a commit of `main` and downloads its tarball in CI (`scripts/translate-js-rust.mjs --fetch`) instead of depending on a version. Section 5 of this issue tracks the publishing machinery. This comment asks for the first release that ships self-translation, even before the remaining rows of this issue are done.
